great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “the Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year… (iii) Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses…”
great.explanation: Automatically reinstates up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year. The recharge can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses, which is very strong for multiple/high-value claims.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: “In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced at same rate at which it is accrued at the commencement of next Policy Year;”
great.explanation: If a claim happens, the accrued No Claims Bonus is reduced at the same rate at which it was accrued, instead of resetting to zero. This helps you retain part of your accumulated increase in Sum Insured even after a claim.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 48 months of continuous coverage…”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are covered only after 48 months of continuous coverage. This is within the common 2–4 year range, so plan for out-of-pocket costs for PED treatment during this period.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage…”
good.explanation: Listed conditions/surgeries are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. Claims for these conditions in the first 2 years can be rejected even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident…”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period, so avoid buying the policy right before planned treatment.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “for a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 60 days immediately before hospital admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “for a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the Hospital”
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 90 days immediately after discharge. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for follow-ups, medicines, and recovery-related treatment.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “If the Policy Schedule states 'up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day' as eligible Room Rent, it means the maximum eligible Room Rent… is limited to 1% of the Sum Insured per day… If the Insured Person is admitted… higher… then… shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses…”
bad.explanation: Room rent can be capped (e.g., up to 1% of Sum Insured per day) if stated in the Policy Schedule. If you choose a higher room category, you may face proportionate (ratable) deductions on associated medical expenses, increasing your share of the bill.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.reference: Clause 4.2 Specific Exclusions (Permanent Exclusions) point 1 + Annexure I
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical/consumables in Annexure I are excluded from cover. This can add meaningful out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization for commonly billed items.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “The Co-payment proportion (if applicable)… (if Age… is 61 Years or above… shall bear a Co-payment of 20% per Claim…)”
bad.explanation: A 20% co-payment per claim applies if the insured person’s age is 61 years or above. This means you must pay 20% of every admissible claim amount yourself, which can be expensive for large hospital bills.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “For an updated list of Network Providers… the Insured Person may refer to the list of Network Providers available on the Company's website or at the call center.”
unclear.explanation: Cashless availability depends on the insurer’s current network provider list published on its website/call center. Since the policy does not state the number of network hospitals, you should verify network strength in your city before buying.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
